title: Communist Pemphlet Entitled The Vanguard, Issue No. 12, Dated 10.3.33, Containing

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
& S. B. REGISTRY
File No. D 4723
S.2./Sp. Br./1933
Date April 5, 1933.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT

Subject (in full) Communist pamphlet entitled "The Vanguard", issue No.12,
dated 10.3.33, containing "Regulations Governing the
Secrecy of Party Activities".

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [Signature] S.I.

I forward herewith, together with translation,
an extract from a copy of a communist pamphlet entitled
"The Vanguard", issue No.12, dated 10.3.33, purporting
to have emanated from the Kiangsu Provincial Committee
of the Chinese Communist Youth Group, which was obtained
by Agent A-3472 in Chapei on April 4, 1933.

A rough summary of the facts in this report and
papers attached were forwarded to Supt. Robertson to be
used as the basis for writing a paragraph on the subject
in case he considered it necessary to refer to it in the
Daily Intelligence Summary.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

S2, Please condemn (obtain)
The Vanguard and other regular secret
publications of the C.C.P. as often as
they come out.
[Signature]
APR 5 1933

D.I. Kuh.
as indicated by o/c S.B.
[Signature] SBR 14/4.

(左侧批注)
Reg:
Noted and passed
to Registry.
Kuh
14/4

Translation of an extract from a communist pamphlet entitled
"The Vanguard", Issue No.12, dated 10.3.33, purporting to
have emanated from the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the
Chinese Communist Youth Group, which was found by the
Municipal Police in Chapei on April 4,1933.

REGULATIONS GOVERNING THE SECRECY OF PARTY ACTIVITIES

(1) That an alarm signal be installed at every 'organization'
and that such signals should be simple and not to be
easily detected by 'enemies'.

(2) That the furnishing of houses correspond to that
of the standard of the occupant.

(3) That active members refrain from carrying with him or
her pieces of paper whilst walking on the streets
and that he or she should not be accompanied by
more than one person.

(4) That no conversations on political matters be entered
into on the streets.

(5) That every member guard against being watched by any
possible observer before entering or leaving the
"premises".

(6) That all members be prohibited from conducting
negotiations in public resorts or busy thoroughfares.

(7) That the number of participants at a meeting to be
held in a house, should not exceed five, and that
the duration of the meeting should not exceed
three hours.

(8) That statements be prepared concerning the social
status of the participants prior to the meeting
being held.

(9) That the same meeting place should not be used more
than three times a week.

(10) That comrades be prohibited from walking in twos
on the street.

(11) That the number of personnel of any organization should
not exceed seven.

(12) That in the event of a comrade being arrested, all
organizations with whom he is connected should
carry out an immediate removal.

(13) That a responsible comrade should not participate
in any public function whatsoever.

Kiangsu Provincial Committee
of the
Chinese Communist Youth Group.
